response.output_text: {"externally_confirmed_facts":["`javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory` is a JSSE engine class for producing `TrustManager` objects. The API provides `getInstance` overloads to select an algorithm (and optionally a provider), `init(KeyStore)` and `init(ManagerFactoryParameters)` initialization methods, and `getTrustManagers()`. Calling `getTrustManagers()` before the factory is initialized throws `IllegalStateException`.","The reported wording refers to the documented `TrustManagerFactory.init(KeyStore ks)` event with `ks == null`. The Java API explicitly permits this parameter value: the `ks` parameter is documented as “the key store, or null.” Null is therefore not, by itself, an API-contract violation.","For SunJSSE `PKIX` and `SunX509` implementations, Oracle’s JSSE Reference Guide documents that `init(null)` causes default trust-material discovery. The documented search first considers `javax.net.ssl.trustStore`, then `<java-home>/lib/security/jssecacerts`, then `<java-home>/lib/security/cacerts`; specified absent or inaccessible stores can lead to an empty keystore/default trust manager. This is documented SunJSSE-provider behavior, not a portable behavior guaranteed by the `TrustManagerFactory` API for every provider.","The phrase “whose loading was not observed” is not stated by the `TrustManagerFactory` Java API. The `KeyStore` API generally states that a keystore must be loaded before it can be accessed, unless it was loaded during construction. That general statement does not say that `TrustManagerFactory.init(null)` requires an application to call `KeyStore.load`.","The reviewed CrySL source does not contain `null`, `trustStore`, `cacerts`, `jssecacerts`, or `load`. It declares `generatedKeyStore[keyStore]` and `generatedManagerFactoryParameters[params]` as requirements, but does not define those predicate meanings. Consequently, the rule source itself does not establish that the detector message represents a missing `KeyStore.load(...)` event.","Documented use is to obtain a factory with a supported trust-manager algorithm, initialize it using the form appropriate to the selected provider (`KeyStore` or `ManagerFactoryParameters`), and obtain trust managers after initialization. Oracle’s JSSE guide directs users to consult the provider vendor when it is unclear which initialization method is appropriate.","The Java SE 25 API states that every Java-platform implementation must support the standard `PKIX` `TrustManagerFactory` algorithm. The standard-name documentation describes `PKIX` as producing `X509ExtendedTrustManager` objects that validate certificate chains under PKIX rules and requiring support for `CertPathTrustManagerParameters` initialization.","The reviewed official sources do not describe a null `KeyStore` as misuse and do not prescribe replacing `init(null)` with an explicit keystore-loading sequence. If an application elects to provide explicit trust material, the documented API mechanism is an initialized `KeyStore`; this is documented API usage, not an official remediation mandated merely by use of null.","Oracle’s JDK 25 provider documentation describes SunJSSE `SunX509` as retained for backward compatibility and says it “should no longer be used.” It documents that SunJSSE `PKIX` supports initialization using either a `KeyStore` or `CertPathTrustManagerParameters`, while `SunX509` supports a `KeyStore` but not `ManagerFactoryParameters`. The reviewed material does not provide a step-by-step migration or equivalence guarantee.","In general-purpose applications, Oracle’s provider documentation recommends requesting cryptographic services without naming a provider, because a named provider may not be present on other Java implementations and prevents use of a higher-preference implementation. This guidance does not establish behavior for a particular provider or runtime.","`TrustManagerFactory` itself defines no persisted truststore format. The `KeyStore` documentation says whether keystores are persistent, and their persistence mechanisms, are unspecified; multiple persistence mechanisms and formats may exist. The reviewed official sources provide no truststore-format conversion or automatic migration procedure for changes to the factory algorithm or initialization mode.","The reviewed `TrustManagerFactory` sources do not define TLS wire formats, enabled protocols, or negotiated protocols. `SSLContext` is the separate JSSE API representing a secure-socket protocol implementation. No reviewed source says that changing `TrustManagerFactory` initialization changes TLS protocol negotiation.","`TrustManagerFactory` has existed since Java 1.4. In the reviewed Java SE 25 documentation, `PKIX` is required; availability of other algorithm names is provider- and implementation-dependent.","The CrySL source’s governing type declaration is, verbatim, `SPEC javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory`. Its event and order clauses are, verbatim: `EVENTS\\n\\tg1: getInstance(algorithm);\\n\\tg2: getInstance(algorithm, _);\\n\\tGet := g1 | g2;\\n\\n\\ti1: init(keyStore);\\n\\ti2: init(params);\\n\\tInit := i1 | i2;\\n\\n\\tgtm1: trustManager = getTrustManagers();\\n\\tGetTrustMng := gtm1;\\n\\nORDER\\n\\tGet, Init, GetTrustMng?`.","The CrySL source does constrain the declared parameter-list shapes: `getInstance` has either one `algorithm` argument or two arguments with `_` as the second; `init` has exactly one declared `keyStore` or `params` argument; and `getTrustManagers` has no declared arguments and is assigned to `trustManager`. The source’s literal constraint is, verbatim, `algorithm in {\"PKIX\", \"SunX509\"};`.","The CrySL source additionally states, verbatim: `REQUIRES\\n\\tgeneratedKeyStore[keyStore];\\n\\tgeneratedManagerFactoryParameters[params];\\n\\nENSURES\\n\\tgeneratedTrustManager[this] after Init;\\n\\tgeneratedTrustManagers[trustManager] after GetTrustMng;`.","Because the source is explicitly a `SPEC javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory`, it does not state a global name-only rule for every method named `getInstance`, `init`, or `getTrustManagers`. A method merely sharing one of those names is not identified by this source itself as a match.
